newsitem.title: FRANCE: Daewoo to put Euro HQ in Paris - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo to put Euro HQ in Paris - paper.

text.p: Daewoo chairman Kim Woo choong said that if his Daewoo Electronics subsidiary were awarded control of Thomson Multimedia he would almost certainly install the Daewoo group's European headquarters in Paris, daily Le Figaro reported on Thursday.
"The decision in 90 percent made," Kim told the paper in an interview. "It could happen next year."

The comments were the latest in the Korean company's efforts to placate criticism from unions and some politicians of the French government's decision to sell Thomson Multimedia to the Korean group as part of the Thomson SA privatisation.
On Wednesday, the company ran full-page advertisements in French newspapers trying to win over opposition and the company has promised to create at least 5,000 jobs in the years to come.
Franck Borotra, French industry minister, told Le Figaro that the company had repeated the pledge, promising to create "at least" 5,200 jobs and "at most" 9,400 in the next five years.

In an attempt to counter some of the most vociferous criticism of the deal, which raises the fear that the sale of Thomson Multimedia would mean handing over what is seen in France as precious digital television technology to a foreign company, Kim said the technology would not be mishandled.
"Just because we buy Thomson doesn't mean we can do just anything with its technology. It belongs to Thomson. We'll have to pay for it," Kim said. "Thomson Multimedia is an excellent company."

Kim said allowing his company to take over Thomson Multimedia would encourage other Korean companies to invest in France and would provide an opportunity to increase diplomatic and industrial cooperation between the two countries.
"The decision to choose France was taken based on concrete facts, economic fundamentals and in a very careful manner," he said in Le Figaro.
"But even if the privatisation commission decided something besides what was preferred by the government, we will continue to follow our policy. France will always stay our partner."
He added that he was "very surprised" by the anti Daewoo reaction in France.
